title: Simple Polyacrylamide-based Multiwell Stiffness Assay for the Study of Stiffness-dependent Cell Responses
protocol: Mix acrylamide (40% w/v) with bisacrylamide (2% w/v) and de-ionized water in the volume percentages specified in Table 1.
Store polyacrylamide gel precursor solution at 4 °C for up to several months.
Prepare N-Sulfosuccinimidyl-6-(4'-azido-2'-nitrophenylamino) hexanoate (Sulfo-SANPAH) aliquots upon receipt.
Store Sulfo-SANPAH aliquots at -20 °C.
Reconstitute sulfo-SANPAH in DMSO at a concentration of 50 mg/ml.
Aliquot the stock solution into tubes containing 20 μl each.
Flash freeze aliquots on dry ice or liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.
Thaw an aliquot briefly when needed.
Dilute thawed sulfo-SANPAH in 480 μl of de-ionized water immediately for use.
Prepare a 10% w/v solution of ammonium persulfate by dissolving it in deionized water.
Aliquot and store the diluted solution at -20 °C until use.
Thaw an aliquot of ammonium persulfate just before use.
Dilute collagen stock to prepare a 0.2 mg/ml solution in PBS with pH 7.4.
Store the diluted collagen solution on ice briefly or use immediately after dilution.
Place a few drops of hydrophobic solution on a glass plate.
Spread the solution across the surface using tissue paper.
Allow the coating to air dry completely.
Wipe the surface again with tissue paper to even out the coating.
Store the hydrophobic solution in a flammable cabinet at room temperature.
Cut flexible plastic support to match the size of the hydrophobic-coated glass plate.
Mark the hydrophobic side of the flexible plastic support by lightly scratching the surface with a scalpel.
Place 4972.5 μl of polyacrylamide precursor solution into a 50 ml conical tube.
Place the tube in a degassing chamber for 30 minutes with the cap open.
Add 25 µl of 10% w/v ammonium persulfate to achieve a final concentration of 0.05%.
Add 2.5 µl of TEMED to the degassed gel solution to achieve a final concentration of 0.5%.
Mix the solution gently by pipetting up and down 3 – 5 times.
Pipette the gel solution onto the hydrophilic side of the flexible plastic support.
Sandwich the support with a hydrophobic-coated glass slide.
Separate the two slides with silicone spacers of desired thickness.
Leave a small amount (~100 μl) of polymer precursor solution in the 50 ml conical tube as an indicator of gelation.
Place another glass plate atop the flexible plastic support/gel sandwich to ensure an even hydrogel surface upon polymerization.
Let the gel polymerize for 45 minutes.
Observe the remaining solution in the 50 ml conical tube to check if it has gelled, indicating initiation of gelation on the glass plate.
Avoid premature opening of the mold to prevent incomplete polymerization.
Once fully polymerized, peel off the flexible plastic support with the covalently attached polyacrylamide gel and set it gel-side-up to air dry.
Dry the gel using convection or heat drying to accelerate the process if needed.
Mark any bare spots on the flexible plastic support where polyacrylamide gels did not form due to bubbles, while the gel is still hydrated.
Cut dried polyacrylamide gels into desired shapes using a heavy-duty hole punch for 96-well plates with a diameter of ~6 mm or use scissors and a paper cutter for other shapes.
Prepare approximately 500 μl of PDMS per 96-well plate according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Place a small droplet (~5 μl) of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) at the center of each well.
Using forceps, place one polyacrylamide gel in each well with the flexible plastic support side down.
Leave the assembled plate at 37 °C for a minimum of 4 hr to allow PDMS to cure.
Place a small amount (7 – 8 μl) of sulfo-SANPAH in each well and swirl from side to side to coat the gel surface evenly.
Place the well plate under a high intensity UV lamp (intensity = 37 mW, λ = 302 – 365 nm) for 5 min.
Rinse the gels with PBS to remove excess sulfo-SANPAH.
Pipette 50 µl of 0.2 mg/ml Collagen Type I solution into each well.
Leave the plate covered at RT for at least 2 hr or O/N at 4 °C to allow collagen bonding.
Rinse with PBS to remove excess collagen solution.
Sterilize under UV (λ = 200 nm) in a tissue culture hood for 2 hr.
Soak the gels in complete medium overnight to hydrate and equilibrate.
Use hydrated gels for cell seeding immediately or store in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Collect cells from tissue culture flask by exposing them to 5% trypsin/EDTA for 5 min at 37 °C.
Re-suspend collected cells in complete medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin at a desired final cell concentration.
Ensure added medium is sufficient to completely submerge the hydrogels.
Count cells under an inverted microscope using a hemacytometer.
Load 10 µl of cell suspension into each hemacytometer port.
Average the cell count from at least 8 quadrants.
Multiply the average cell count by 104 to get the final cell concentration.
Culture cells onto the PA stiffness assay in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change media every 2 – 3 days during culture.
Collect cells when needed by exposing them to 5% trypsin/EDTA at 37 °C for 5 min.
Use approximately 80 μl of trypsin/EDTA per cm2 of tissue culture flask.
Aspirate or pipette medium by slightly tipping the multiwell plate sideways and touching the pipette tip onto the side wall of each well during all cell manipulation steps.
Take special care not to disrupt the hydrogel surface during standard tissue culture handling.
Image cells directly on the PA stiffness assay using any type of microscope.
Position PA stiffness assay in microscope plate holder and image for live cell imaging.
Keep imaging sessions under 2 hr, or use a microscope equipped with an environmental chamber for longer imaging times.
Fix cells in 4% formaldehyde solution supplemented with 0.1% detergent when live cell imaging is not the goal.
Soak cells in fixative at RT for a minimum of 2 hr.
Rinse with PBS twice after fixation.
Discard fixative waste in a designated waste container.
Store fixed cells submerged in PBS at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks if imaging is delayed.
Stain fixed cells with desired cell stain directly in the multiwell plate for fluorescent imaging.
Image stained cells immediately.
